newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Savings Bank plans move into Lithuania.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Savings Bank plans move into Lithuania.

text.p: Estonia's second-largest bank, Savings Bank, said on Friday that it was planning a move into Lithuania, the southernmost Baltic state, either by buying a controlling share of a bank or by starting its own bank.
Heino Viik, the deputy director of the bank's financial division, said the bank's supervisory board was to finalise its plans at a meeting later this month.
He made the comments after a local news agency, the Baltic News Service (BNS), reported that Savings Bank had bought shares in Lithuanian bank Ukio Bankas.
Viik said the stake was under 10 percent.
"There are different possibilities," Viik told Reuters of the bank's plans to expand into Lithuania.
"Of course one scenario is to buy a bank, or shall we say a controlling stake, and the other is to start a new bank there."
Estonian banks have been the most aggressive in expanding out of their small home market of 1.5 million people and into the neighbouring Baltic countries.
Leading bank Hansapank has already bought a bank in Latvia and also says it wants to enter the Lithuanian market.
An Estonian investment firm, Talinvest, recently bought a share in a Lithuanian brokerage, Suprema.
